steps.content: In the evening, at the cafe on the street corner, the woman puts down her coffee cup and starts scrolling on the device.
With a casual swipe, she quickly skims through a bunch of data, occasionally keying in a few commands to allow her antennae to reach the target through several proxies and decoys.
By the time she finishes half of her coffee, she's already breached the official firewall as if it was made of paper and taken over the entire building's system.
She switches between several surveillance cameras and finally finds what she wants to see.
On the screen, the old woman sleeps quietly on the hospital bed, surrounded by medical equipment. These are the tools that can both sustain her life and end everything.
The command to end it all has already been written. All it takes is a single tap on the phone screen. All troubles will be resolved, all truths buried.
Her finger hovers in mid-air. This momentary pause isn't enough to determine if she has any hesitation. The next second, the button is pressed, and the command sent.

steps.speaker: Moore
steps.content: ...It's over.
She puts down the phone and gazes up aimlessly at the passersby on the street.
[Transition] 1 second
The afternoon sunlight gradually turns into the evening sunset, the same blood-red hue spilling over her. The pedestrians on the street slowly dwindle.
Until they've all silently disappeared, even the cafe's servers are nowhere to be seen. The woman sits still and has folded up her device unusually, simply watching the street quietly.
When the cold coffee in her cup is finally gone, someone comes over to her.
Mind if I sit here? I'll buy you a coffee.

steps.speaker: Moore
steps.content: Hmm, thank you.

steps.speaker: Moore
steps.content: Why are you here? How are things at the hospital? Is Granny Henie alright?

steps.speaker: Choice
options: She's the same as before. Don't worry.

choices.text: She's the same as before. Don't worry.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: After all, she's an important witness. I'll let no one harm her. Before the suspect made a move, I had already gathered quite a bit of interesting information.
You say as you put a stack of paper documents on the table, pushing them to her.
Moore doesn't pick them up but keeps smiling at you, like a teacher patiently waiting for an answer from her student.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Mr. Bruce was involved in the investigation of the DisCity dark web from N.F. 106 to N.F. 109. He was very committed and led the task force with plenty of achievements, but three of his colleagues ended up with death threats from the dark web.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Bruce, however, remained unharmed as their technical backbone. This continued until N.F. 109 when Granny Henie was diagnosed with a chronic mental illness, pushing the couple to step down from their key positions and prioritize their family.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: A year passed from then and by N.F. 110, he had stopped participating in investigative operations and posed no threat to the dark web. Attacks on investigators had also long ceased.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: But around this time, Mr. Bruce died in an attack. In your terms, he was murdered by the forces behind the dark web because he'd crossed a line.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: This prompted me to look into which exact line he crossed.

steps.speaker: Moore
steps.content: And did you find out?

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: The DisCity dark web's methods are very sophisticated. Any recordable information or evidence has likely been taken care of. I was only able to gather some obscure accounts.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: In N.F. 110, before being killed, Bruce desperately sought out some friends, saying he couldn't reach his kid and was worried she'd run into danger at work. Some even said... he couldn't wait for the authorities and had to look for her himself.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: And he never returned since. Logically, I suspect he'd discovered something during the process that led to his murder.

steps.speaker: Moore
steps.content: And what else?
Moore smiles at you, waiting for you to continue.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: You approached this family only to get close to Cybersec. Taking care of Granny Henie was merely an act of charity you put on.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Both assassination and rescue are means you use to conceal the dark web's secrets. You've been working for the dark web from the start, haven't you?
She says nothing, quietly tracing the rim of her coffee cup with her fingertip. After a moment, she replies with a question.

steps.speaker: Moore
steps.content: All this intel is no easy find. You must suspect me more than anyone else does. I can only imagine how determined you were to find the proof of my betrayal.

steps.speaker: Moore
steps.content: Why? Because of those little spiders' advice? Or because that young journalist told you only the strong ones can commit such evil? Or because Elysiland was resolved too easily, making you suspect I'm hiding something?

steps.speaker: Moore
steps.content: Was all my effort to hide the truth futile?

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: I wanted to believe you. I really did. I wished you were innocent. That there was an explanation for everything suspicious about you. That I could gain a strong and reliable partner.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: How I wish it was all just a mistake and false suspicion. That the Bruce couple's death was a mere misfortune and your involvement in the operations was indeed to serve justice. That your care for Granny Henie these past 4 years was genuine.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: That you accepted my proposal to help Granny Henie wake from her nightmare. That you could heal her wounds from her broken family, become her new family, and help her regain happiness in her remaining years.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: I really did hope this guess was true.

steps.speaker: Moore
steps.content: Hehe... Hahaha...
You watch her laugh until her whole body is trembling with it. You watch her wipe away the tears from laughter.

steps.speaker: Moore
steps.content: Be bolder, Chief. Don't just try to pick one correct answer.

steps.speaker: Moore
steps.content: Why can't both be true?
Moore turns to face you, her gaze shifting from the street to you. The fading sunset still beams down on her warm features, yet you suddenly find her face incredibly unfamiliar.

steps.speaker: Moore
steps.content: I never care about anyone, not even myself. But the Bruces were different. I was truly grateful to them.

steps.speaker: Moore
steps.content: On my eighteenth birthday, I had just completed the hardest and most important job my client had given me. According to the rules then, those three who barged into my home at that time shouldn't have lived.

steps.speaker: Moore
steps.content: But I let them go. I thought maybe they were too eager to help me and didn't see what was hidden in that apartment.

steps.speaker: Moore
steps.content: Perhaps... I really wanted to taste that birthday cake.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: But what about four years later? You still did it. You turned your back on those who loved you. You betrayed them and stabbed them with your knife.

steps.speaker: Moore
steps.content: Yes, if only they hadn't crossed the line, hadn't discovered my real job... What a shame.

steps.speaker: Moore
steps.content: N.F. 110, four years ago, the council election year... Of course, the DisCity dark web had a job to do during this important event. I got assigned many tasks to support my work partners. I was working late for several days in a row, too busy to go home.

steps.speaker: Moore
steps.content: To save the Bruces from having to worry about me, I made up excuses and fake tasks at Cybersec, covered my traces, and kept the server somewhere outside so I could concentrate on my work.

steps.speaker: Moore
steps.content: But still, my teachers, mentors, and parents, the Bruces, were too good to be fooled by me. They found me. I was too tired from working so I let my guard down. I slipped up and let them see things they shouldn't have seen.
Even though you anticipated this answer, a chill still goes down your spine.

steps.speaker: Moore
steps.content: Come to think of it, it's truly a shame.

steps.speaker: Moore
steps.content: If I hadn't overworked myself to the point of losing track of time, if I had come home on time, they wouldn't have been so worried or thought I got into trouble with some dark web hitman.

steps.speaker: Moore
steps.content: If they had been less smart and tech-savvy, if they hadn't tracked me down so fast and cracked my device... they wouldn't have seen what they shouldn't have seen.

steps.speaker: Moore
steps.content: If they could have cared less about a strange girl and stopped coming after me and trying to get to the bottom of it... I wouldn't have had to do it.

steps.speaker: Moore
steps.content: How I wish...
Moore stops with her hypothetical scenarios. She looks back at you. You can't tell if there's more regret or irony in her smile.

steps.speaker: Moore
steps.content: Sadly, every if/else condition led to the worst option out of the two. I was accountable to my client after all, and I had no choice but to do it.

steps.speaker: Moore
steps.content: The only consolation was that... Granny Henie went mad. She probably didn't want to face the reality, and to face me, the person who killed her entire family.

steps.speaker: Moore
steps.content: It's good that she's lost her mind... I'll stay to take care of her. And I get to keep my only family. If she really defied the odds and gained back her senses, I would have to go through the trouble of doing it a third time.

steps.speaker: Moore
steps.content: If only you hadn't shown up and ruined everything, Chief.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Enough about this family. Now answer my questions.

steps.speaker: Choice
options: You're the mastermind behind the dark web.

choices.text: You're the mastermind behind the dark web.

steps.content: Her smile deepens. She dips her head slightly, the reflection on her glasses obscuring her eyes. She speaks as if the program has finally received the correct command.

steps.speaker: Moore
steps.content: Yes, and its creator too. The DisCity dark web is an engineering feat I'm quite satisfied with. It's a gift for my independent life, and I've completed many projects with it.

steps.speaker: Choice
options: You killed everyone who discovered the truth.

steps.speaker: Moore
steps.content: Yes. I'm willing to be accountable to my client.

steps.speaker: Choice
options: What have you done using the dark web?

choices.text: What have you done using the dark web?

steps.speaker: Moore
steps.content: I've signed an NDA. But don't worry, you'll find out soon enough.

steps.speaker: Choice
options: Who is your client? The Underground?

choices.text: Who is your client? The Underground?

steps.speaker: Moore
steps.content: It's confidential. But rest assured, she'll come to see you sooner or later.
She looks at you, blinks once, and suddenly smiles.

steps.speaker: Moore
steps.content: Pfft, haha... What a cute question.

steps.speaker: Moore
steps.content: Oh, sorry, my bad. You asked the right question. You deserve a reward.
The cafe's lights explode suddenly. You stand up quickly to pull away from her while countless laser beams come from afar, aiming at Moore.
You hear her laughter in the dark and watch as she slowly unbuttons her collar, revealing a red birthmark-like pattern on her chest.
Except it's not a birthmark... It's twisting and writhing like a living thing, resembling a grotesquely beautiful flower.
In that moment, you remember something.

steps.speaker: Moore
steps.content: Doesn't it look familiar? You should have seen this flower before in my data.

The flower seems capable of devouring your consciousness. The more you gaze at it, the deeper you feel trapped by it. Your vision starts writhing as if a nonexistent force is gradually gathering, converging on the human who bears the flower.
Moore smiles slightly, and beside her, the light screen that has protected you many times rises, now covered in sharp, glowing spikes. This time, though, it has turned into a menacing weapon.

steps.speaker: Moore
steps.content: I could make up a thousand reasons to let Bruce live, but because he discovered this... it couldn't be helped.

steps.speaker: Moore
steps.content: I can't break my contract with the one who planted this flower.

steps.speaker: Moore
steps.content: Now, you've seen everything you should and shouldn't have seen. Got any final questions?
Around the street corner, figures in trench coats and hats begin emerging. Soon, the crowd surrounds the cafe.
The 9th Agency, the MBCC, the FAC, special agents, soldiers, Sinners... There hasn't been a battle of this scale in a long time. The confrontation escalates in no time.
Everyone understands that the person facing you is no longer an ordinary Sinner... It's an enemy with which no negotiation is possible.

steps.speaker: Choice
options: You said a part of you died in N.F. 110.

choices.text: You said a part of you died in N.F. 110.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: It sounded disgustingly genuine.

steps.speaker: Moore
steps.content: Because I was trying to fool you, silly.

steps.speaker: Moore
steps.content: I'm glad you once believed in my humanity. Even if you didn't buy into it completely, it still pleases me.

steps.speaker: Moore
steps.content: After all, when I killed that kind couple, even I didn't believe I had a heart.
Explosions break out one after another. Surging flames illuminate the city in the evening.
You've known from the start this showdown was inevitable.

█/█ 
MBCC Chief's Office
The series of sensational dark web cases has come to an end.
With the clues left at the scene, the 9th Agency and other departments soon discovered the location of the dark web's main server and successfully destroyed it.
As for the culprit, Sinner Moore, she disappeared in the explosions during the battle, leaving behind no remains. But since the shackles between you two have vanished, she is considered dead.
Moore's colleagues, the medical staff at the nursing home, and those who had interacted with her at the Bureau have all shown varying degrees of grief and sadness.
With the election approaching, Eastside's political scene has never been more active. Multiple councilors have begun their campaigns on the streets.
In a matter of days, both the media and the general public have lost interest in the dark web.

DisCity has always been this way. No one would pay attention to something that no longer poses a threat or an interest. However detrimental it once was to this city, it is now nothing more than just a few cold lines of text in the records.
[Transition to the Underground]

steps.speaker: Dark Voice
steps.content: Moore has been exposed.
Is that so? What a pity.

steps.speaker: Dark Voice
steps.content: No matter, her mission is already finished. Under her cover, the three other plans have been progressing steadily.

steps.speaker: Dark Voice
steps.content: She insisted on staying above ground four years ago for some reason. Now that she has nowhere else to go, she can finally return without hesitation.
What about the shackles? The defective one has imposed those shackles on her. Won't they attract those people from DisCity?

steps.speaker: Dark Voice
steps.content: Don't fret. The shackles have already been severed by ███. Surely the power of that defective one is no match for more superior power.

steps.speaker: Dark Voice
steps.content: The Overgrounders will only think that the dark web's master is dead. The best way to get rid of a chasing hound is to throw it some bones, am I right?

steps.speaker: Dark Voice
steps.content: That's exactly that woman's favorite trick. See how she threw out that useless server to distract those investigators.
[Transition to the Bureau]

On TV, some media have found Moore's parents and are trying to dig out more news. But what they get is nothing new to you: Moore's parents are still alive, but they have long since formed new families and even forgotten they had a daughter. They haven't seen her once in nearly twenty years.
Facing the pressing questions, they both give the same cold and pointless answer.

steps.speaker: Moore's Family
steps.content: I have no idea why she turned out this way. She has nothing to do with me. I don't do interviews.

steps.speaker: Moore's Family
steps.content: Unless... we can get a share of the insurance money?
[Transition to the Underground]

steps.speaker: Dark Voice
steps.content: Hehehe, as long as they are satisfied. Isn't that what Moore wants?

steps.speaker: Dark Voice
steps.content: The dark web... No, Pestilence's mission is fulfilled. Digitalized Mania is fully mature, and physical hardware is no longer needed. Every individual in DisCity who has touched the dark web will become a server for the new Mania network.

steps.speaker: Dark Voice
steps.content: Let those people in DisCity celebrate and hold onto that useless wreckage for now. Our network has already surpassed disasters and reached the entire world.

steps.speaker: Dark Voice
steps.content: The path has already been paved. The wheels will move forward and nothing will stop them now. Next...

steps.speaker: 9th
steps.content: Chief, you look a bit uneasy. Don't you want to join the celebration of this rare victory?

steps.speaker: 9th
steps.content: We've finally tracked down the source of the dark web and eliminated the uncertainty that's been plaguing us. The shackles of the mastermind have been broken too. You should let go of whatever premonition you have and just relax for a moment.

steps.speaker: 9th
steps.content: Or else... how can we face the upcoming war?

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: You're right. It's just that...
You suddenly remember there's still a place you must visit.
[Transition to the Underground]
It's finally over
I can take some time off
So where should I go next?
The thoughts are suddenly interrupted by the image of that home, the fire, the burned car, the white sheet, and...

steps.speaker: Henie
steps.content: Who... are you...

steps.speaker: Henie
steps.content: It was you who took them away, wasn't it...

steps.speaker: Henie
steps.content: Where are they?! Bring them back! Give me back my kids!
[Black Screen]

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: You said a part of you died in N.F. 110. It sounded... disgustingly genuine.

steps.speaker: Moore
steps.content: ...Hehe. Of course, I was only fooling you, silly.

steps.speaker: Moore
steps.content: Longing, guilt, or a belated sense of humanity... These things don't exist in me. It was only a line of code containing an error that I didn't bother to correct for years, which finally died just now.

steps.speaker: Moore
steps.content: Thanks for helping me spot this little anomaly. Well then...

steps.speaker: Moore
steps.content: The next time we meet, don't expect the same leniency, Chief.
[Hospital]
Back at the hospital, you see Granny Henie lying quietly on the hospital bed. You have not yet reached an agreement on whether to proceed with the surgery, and no one can make this decision for her.
And that murder command you intercepted back then... was somewhat different from what you'd imagined. It didn't contain any digitalized Mania either.
It couldn't even be called a command, for it was just a simple, plain message:
<size=44>Have a sweet dream, Granny Henie</size>
